summary.prose: Building this Story gives the tracker port a status read, then uses it two ways: a deadline-bound refresh that the git_pull and git_push tools run after success (and the tracker.sync method runs on request), and issue creation at first draft for repos with no team policy when the tracker is on. The chain report also shows the issue key, artifact id and revision. The work ends with the amendments, the documentation and one full sweep.

tasks.title: Build the deadline-bound refresh and route tracker.sync through it
tasks.summary: Add refreshTrackerStatus(repoPath, { epicHash?, deadline? }) with TRACKER_REFRESH_DEADLINE_MS (120 s) and rebuild syncTracker over the port, keeping the SyncResult shape (synced, skipped, failed) unchanged so the terminal client and existing sync tests keep working: the Deadline is checked before every read, its signal is passed to the registry calls through workflowToolDeps so a call in flight is cancelled, an adapter without status-read is a failed result naming the capability, a ToolDenied is rethrown, other failures and the deadline are skipped or failed results with one warning line each. The tracker.sync daemon method returns the SyncResult of the one Epic through the same function (repoPath stays required and names an absolute registered repo).

tasks.title: Register the two post-success hooks on git_pull and git_push
tasks.summary: Register tracker-refresh-after-pull and tracker-refresh-after-push at daemon start (registerToolHook, the first production rules). A rule acts only when input.cwd is present and equals the registered repository root exactly after canonicalising both paths; a linked worktree, including the detached temporary worktree the handoff park pushes from, is refused because its cwd differs from the registered path (confirmed by comparing git_rev_parse gitDir with the common directory). The pull must not be a dry run and the push must have data.pushed true. The rule calls refreshTrackerStatus with its own Deadline (the hook receives no signal) and throws one line when the refresh was skipped, failed or denied, so the executor reports it as hookFailures while the git tool stays a success.
acceptanceChecks: a successful non-dry-run pull and a pushed push in a registered repo root refresh the status
a dry run, a push with pushed false, a missing cwd and a linked worktree run no refresh
a push from a temporary worktree (the handoff park) runs no refresh
a failing, denied or slow tracker leaves the tool a success and adds hookFailures and a line of output

syncTracker and refreshTrackerStatus over a fake port: success writes epicStatus, storyStatus and lastSyncedAt only; a port without status-read fails naming the capability; a read that fails is a failed result; no bound issue is skipped; a fake port that is slow on every read hits the 120-second budget with an injected Deadline and the unread Epics and Stories are reported skipped with 'time limit reached'; a ToolDenied is rethrown

missingCapabilities reports status-read for a declared set without it; the existing capability-set assertions in src/workflow/tracker/__tests__/port.test.ts and github-adapter.test.ts are updated to include status-read

git_pull and git_push through callTool with the two hooks registered: a successful run is followed by a refresh; a failing tracker leaves success true and adds hookFailures and a line of output; a ToolDenied from the refresh is reported the same way; a dry-run pull, a dry-run push (success with pushed false) and a failed git command run no refresh
